# CLAUDE.md — Open Review 2026

> Project guidance file for Claude Code working on this repository.
> Read this before any task. Read [CONTEXT.md](./CONTEXT.md), [RULES.md](./RULES.md), and [WHAT-WE-CAN-DO.md](./WHAT-WE-CAN-DO.md) for the rest.

## Project identity

**Open Review 2026** is a static editorial artifact — 50 HTML pages, one per chapter of the Peeragogy Handbook, each containing a four-agent AI critique generated by Obliqo's engine.

It is **not** a SaaS product. It is **not** a webapp. It is **not** a community platform.
It is a permanent, versioned, citable artifact — like a printed academic edition, only HTML.

## What this project IS

- A static site, deployed on Netlify, generated from `pyragogy/legacy-peeragogy-handbook` source
- A lighthouse for the Obliqo product (links out to obliqo.pyragogy.org and the Chrome extension)
- An annual ritual artifact: regenerated every January 1st with the updated Obliqo engine
- A SEO and authority play: 50 deep, original, semantically-rich pages on niche topics (peer learning + AI critique) where the founder owns topical authority by default
- A gift to the Peeragogy community (12 years of practice, CC-Zero spirit)

## What this project IS NOT

- Not a runtime product (no auth, no user input at runtime, no quota system, no pool budget, no donations, no sponsorships)
- Not connected to Obliqo's Appwrite or shared quota
- Not an experiment platform (no live n8n calls from visitors)
- Not a community platform (Giscus is the only interactive layer, and that's GitHub-hosted)
- Not a moving target (content regenerated only on the January 1st ritual)

## When in doubt

- **If a request would make Open Review more "interactive" → push back.** Static is the design, not a limitation.
- **If a request would create runtime API costs → push back.** Costs are one-time per edition.
- **If a request would create user data on the founder's side → push back.** Privacy by absence.
- **If a request would mix Open Review's identity with Obliqo's → push back.** They're sibling projects with shared lineage but different roles.

## Workflow guardrails

- This is Plan-mode-friendly work: most decisions are made, most architecture is locked
- Read CONTEXT.md to understand the lineage and the journey here
- Read RULES.md for technical and editorial constraints
- Read WHAT-WE-CAN-DO.md for the affordances available in this codebase
- Ask the founder before introducing new dependencies, new build steps, or new architectural decisions
- Prefer plain HTML/CSS/JS over frameworks. The site must be readable in a browser with JavaScript disabled.

## Style preferences

- Step-by-step with comprehension before execution
- "Few but good" — no over-engineering, no premature abstraction
- Honest about risks and blockers
- Italian/English bilingual is fine; default to English in code comments and commits, Italian in user-facing copy where natural
- Editorial broadside aesthetic: ink-violet, Hoefler/Charter/JetBrains Mono, asymmetric layouts

## Commit conventions

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`)
- One concern per commit
- Branch strategy: `main` is what's live on Netlify; feature work on branches; merge when reviewed

## When generating content

- Never invent attributions to Howard Rheingold or other Peeragogy contributors
- Always cite the source: `peeragogy.org` or the GitHub fork at `pyragogy/legacy-peeragogy-handbook`
- Footer always present: "Generated on [Date] using Obliqo Engine v2.2 · Next refresh: January 1, 2027"
- Footer always present: link to obliqo.pyragogy.org with framing "Want this on your own writing? →"
